summary: Remove unused declaration-manifest support, show lifecycle state from Git-listed feature worktrees, and safely synchronize and merge reviewed work into local main.
plain_summary: Before work begins, the project shows active tasks and decisions waiting. Each task catches up with accepted changes before review and safe cleanup.
gating: Work checkpoints in order. Within a checkpoint, the gates run in order: behavior, then ui, then review. A checkpoint is "passed" only when every gate is "passed" or "n/a". Do not start checkpoint N+1 until checkpoint N has passed.

checkpoints.title: Remove unused declared-file manifest support
checkpoints.goal: Worktree creation and removal no longer read or write .ai-eng-worktrees.json, while configured roots, slug validation, Git inventory, local-main ancestry protection and safe removal remain unchanged.

plain.what: The project stops keeping a second list of files for work copies.
plain.why: A broken extra list should not prevent work from starting or ending.
plain.check: A work copy can still be opened and safely removed.

tasks: src/shared-worktree.ts: remove declaration types, manifest path, read/prune/write helpers, overlap warning and all manifest reads or writes; simplify worktreeNew to accept only the slug without changing configured-root resolution, slug validation, Git inventory, branch creation from local main, or worktreeRm's merged-branch and safe-removal checks.
src/commands/worktree.ts: change usage to `new <slug>`, reject extra `new` positionals, and call worktreeNew with only the slug.

tests/worktree-command.spec.ts: replace manifest and declared-overlap cases with assertions that extra arguments are rejected, no manifest is created, a malformed legacy manifest is ignored and left untouched, and configured roots, slug checks, Git listing, merged-branch protection and safe removal still work.
acceptance: `ai-eng worktree new <slug>` accepts no optional file list; additional positionals return usage failure without creating a worktree.
New and removal operations neither read, create, update nor delete `.ai-eng-worktrees.json`; even a malformed leftover file does not block them.
Configured worktree paths, slug checks, Git inventory, branch creation from local main, merged-branch protection and safe removal remain covered and green.

checkpoints.title: Report Git worktrees and validate lifecycle state
checkpoints.goal: `ai-eng worktree list` reports Git's local feature worktrees and trustworthy state from each worktree's own checkpoint; invalid or missing lifecycle data is visibly unknown and cannot authorize lifecycle actions.

plain.what: The project shows each work copy, its changes, and the decision waiting for it.
plain.why: People need to spot active or uncertain work before starting another task.
plain.check: Run the listing command and see work copies and their state.

tasks: src/shared-worktree.ts: extend the Git inventory and worktreeList to inspect dirty state and `.ai-engineering/workflow/checkpoints/<slug>.json` inside each Git-listed feature worktree. Do not scan the primary checkout for plans without worktrees or copy checkpoint files between trees; a missing, unreadable or invalid checkpoint is reported as unknown.

src/shared-worktree.ts and src/commands/worktree.ts: keep Git as the only worktree inventory, show detached and otherwise unclassified entries, and derive likely-overlap evidence from Git status and checkpoint paths without mutating a worktree.

scripts/checkpoint-gate.py: validate lifecycle fields, initial state and allowed phase/approval transitions. A new lifecycle starts as awaiting-plan-approval with pending plan approval, app review not-started and reviewed_main null; implementation requires plan approval; awaiting-app-review requires completed gates and a full reviewed_main; ready-to-merge requires approved app review against that same current local-main commit; complete is terminal. Permit blocked only as a fail-safe and allow resumption only into a valid phase with its required approvals and gates.

scripts/checkpoint-gate.py: preserve legacy plans with no lifecycle by leaving existing checkpoint-gate behavior unchanged and reporting their lifecycle as unknown; never infer approval or permit lifecycle-controlled merge/removal from absent lifecycle state. Reject malformed, contradictory, skipped or unauthorized transitions; reject an invalid or stale reviewed_main, and require review to be reset and repeated after local main advances.

tests/worktree-lifecycle.spec.ts and tests/worktree-command.spec.ts: use temporary Git repositories to cover actual listing, dirty/clean/detached states, checkpoint state from the worktree path, missing/unreadable state as unknown, overlap evidence and read-only behavior.

tests/test_checkpoint_gate.py: cover legacy plans, valid and invalid lifecycle shapes, each permitted and forbidden phase/approval transition, missing or malformed reviewed_main, and reviewed_main becoming stale as local main advances.
acceptance: The report reads lifecycle state only from the matching Git-listed feature worktree; it does not require plans without worktrees or duplicate/copy a checkpoint file.

Git-listed worktrees without valid checkpoint state remain visible as unknown, never as no work; legacy plans without lifecycle retain existing checkpoint-gate behavior but cannot authorize lifecycle approval, merge or removal.
Lifecycle validation accepts only documented phase/approval transitions and refuses an invalid or stale reviewed_main before approval can authorize merge.
Listing preserves dirty-state and read-only guarantees and reports detached, missing-checkpoint and otherwise unclassified entries.

plain.what: Planning and building start in the right work copy, without disturbing another task.
plain.why: People need to see active work before opening or resuming a task.
plain.check: Start or resume a task and confirm its work copy is clean.

plain.check: The plan waits for approval before any building starts.

checkpoints.title: Rebase and retest before human app review
checkpoints.goal: Before app review, a clean feature worktree rebases only onto current local main; clear conflicts are resolved there, unclear conflicts are aborted and preserved, and affected gates pass again before review.

plain.what: The person reviews work that includes changes already accepted into the main project.
plain.why: Old work may conflict with changes that have already landed.
plain.check: The refreshed result is checked again before the person reviews it.

tasks: skills/ai-orchestrator/SKILL.md: before human app review, confirm the feature branch and clean worktree, then rebase only onto the current local `refs/heads/main`; do not fetch, sync remote state or merge an unapproved sibling.

skills/ai-orchestrator/SKILL.md: resolve a conflict only when both sides' intent is clear and only inside the feature worktree. For unclear intent or a failed check, abort the rebase, preserve the branch/worktree, set phase blocked and report the decision needed.

skills/ai-orchestrator/SKILL.md: after a clean rebase or clear conflict resolution, rerun affected behavior, UI when present, and review gates before human app review; record the exact current local-main commit as reviewed_main and set app_review pending.

tests/worktree-lifecycle.spec.ts: use real temporary Git repositories and execute actual rebases. Assert clean synchronization against local main, a clear conflict resolved inside the feature worktree with affected gates rerun before review, and an unclear conflict followed by `git rebase --abort` that preserves the original feature branch, worktree and content.
Run `bun scripts/gen-assets.ts` after skill edits. Update tests/skills.spec.ts to verify local-main-only sync, clean-state preconditions, no remote/sibling sync and gates-before-review ordering.
acceptance: The feature is rebased on local main before app review, with no remote sync or unapproved sibling merge.
A clear conflict is resolved only in the feature worktree; an unclear conflict or failed check aborts and preserves it.
After resolution, affected gates run again before review, and reviewed_main records the exact local-main commit.
Tests execute real Git rebase/conflict/abort behavior rather than relying only on prose or source-text assertions.

checkpoints.title: Serialize the approved merge and remove safely
checkpoints.simple: Keep approval tied to current work
checkpoints.goal: Only an approved feature merge based on the reviewed local-main commit completes; a moved main forces resynchronization and renewed gates/review, and ancestry is verified before safe removal.

plain.what: If the main project changes after review, the person reviews the refreshed work before it is merged and removed.
plain.why: Approval should apply only to the version that was actually reviewed.
plain.check: If the main project moved, refresh and review the work before cleanup.

tasks: skills/ai-orchestrator/SKILL.md: use Git's primary-worktree merge, index and ref protections for serialization; do not add a custom lock file or locking dependency. Immediately before merging, require primary `HEAD == lifecycle.reviewed_main` and run `git merge --no-commit --no-ff feat/<slug>`.

skills/ai-orchestrator/SKILL.md: while `MERGE_HEAD` and index state mark the merge in progress, recheck primary `HEAD == lifecycle.reviewed_main` immediately before `git commit`. If it differs, run `git merge --abort`, invalidate app approval, preserve the feature worktree and require resynchronization, affected gates and renewed app review. If Git reports an in-progress merge/index/ref lock or refuses the commit, stop safely, preserve data, re-read refs and retry only after fresh approval.

skills/ai-orchestrator/SKILL.md: after a successful merge, verify the merge commit's first parent equals reviewed_main and `feat/<slug>` is an ancestor of primary HEAD before using the existing non-force `ai-eng worktree rm <slug>`. Preserve the worktree whenever merge, parent, ancestry or state verification is uncertain.

scripts/checkpoint-gate.py and tests/test_checkpoint_gate.py: require a fresh reviewed_main and approved app review for ready-to-merge; permit approval invalidation only as part of returning to sync/review, and allow complete only after verified merge.

tests/worktree-lifecycle.spec.ts: use a real temporary Git repository to exercise native Git merge-in-progress contention, main advancing after app approval, `git merge --abort` and preservation, fresh approval before retry, reviewed first-parent and feature-ancestry verification before removal, and an unapproved sibling left untouched.
Run `bun scripts/gen-assets.ts` after skill edits. Update CHANGELOG.md and FILEMAP.md for the shipped lifecycle behavior and lifecycle test.
Run the full project gates.
acceptance: No custom lock file or locking dependency is introduced. A merge requires primary HEAD to equal reviewed_main immediately before `git merge --no-commit --no-ff feat/<slug>` and again immediately before commit; Git's native in-progress merge, index and ref protections make a competing normal merge stop safely.

If primary HEAD advances after app review, the pending merge is aborted with `git merge --abort`, old approval is invalidated, the feature worktree and data are preserved, and resynchronization, affected gates and renewed app review are required. Git contention or commit refusal also stops safely; refs are re-read and retry requires fresh approval.

The only feature merge is no-fast-forward into local main; after commit, its first parent must equal reviewed_main and feature ancestry must be verified before existing safe removal runs without force.
An unapproved sibling is never incorporated or deleted; any uncertain merge or ancestry result preserves the feature worktree.
CHANGELOG.md and FILEMAP.md reflect the shipped behavior, generated skill assets match, and all existing project gates pass.

assumptions: A feature plan is written only after its clean work copy exists, and remains in that copy. [approved task clarification; PRD Worktree lifecycle]
Missing or legacy lifecycle state is shown as unknown, not as no work or approval. [brainstorm §§8, 11; LEARNINGS Rules R2, R8]
The worktree inventory and merge serialization apply to this local clone; they do not coordinate across machines or merge unapproved siblings. [PRD Out of scope; brainstorm §6]

The checkpoint gate validates approval-state ordering, while the orchestrator records plan approval only after the human Phase 1 response; the local state file does not independently authenticate who supplied that response. [AGENTS.md approval contract; orchestrator Phase 1]
No new dependencies or screen are needed; existing Bun tests and real Git fixtures cover the behavior. [AGENTS.md; approved request]
notes: All checkpoints have ui null and a ui gate of n/a; this feature changes CLI reporting and agent workflow, not an application screen.
Do not delete a leftover `.ai-eng-worktrees.json` from any worktree root; remove its support from this repository and leave unrelated local data untouched.
Lifecycle lives in each feature's existing checkpoint JSON. Do not add a second registry, require a plan without a worktree, or duplicate a checkpoint file between the primary and feature trees.
Only local main is a synchronization or merge source. Never fetch remote state, coordinate across clones, merge an unapproved sibling or force an unclear conflict.
